fine_trace.note: Attacker-controlled reloc_count field is parsed big-endian from the input file header; here set to 1 so the relocs() reloc-table branch is entered.
Attacker-controlled reloc_start is parsed from the input header; set to 0x1000, far beyond the 64-byte file, to force the relocs() error path.
A freshly allocated RList is stored in the bflt object BEFORE any validation of the header fields, so the object now owns a reference to this list.
Because reloc_count == 1 the relocation-table parsing branch is taken, using the attacker-controlled reloc_start value.
reloc_start (0x1000) + amount (4) exceeds the 64-byte file size, so the code frees the temporaries and jumps to out_error.

Root cause: the error path frees the RList that obj->relocs_list still points to, but never resets obj->relocs_list to NULL, leaving a dangling pointer in the bflt object. Safety condition that should hold: after the error path obj->relocs_list == NULL so it is not freed again.
Sink: when the RBinFile is destroyed (r_bin_file_free -> destroy -> r_bin_bflt_free), r_list_free dereferences the already-freed RList, causing a heap-use-after-free READ in r_list_free.
